Integrates multiple dimensions: combines efficacy, toxicity, quality life within unified decision-analytic framework (MAUT), hierarchical aggregation mirrors clinical reasoning: efficacy first, QoL, toxicity. text: function performs following steps: 1.  Prompts user select one five predefined QoL scenarios (e.g., "Significant Improvement"). 2.  Prompts user rate strength evidence scenario 5-point scale. 3.  Calculates confidence factor `alpha` (0 1) based evidence strength. 4. title: Sample Quality of Life (QoL) Scores from a Multinomial Distribution — sample_qol_scores
code: # --- 1. Define a probability vector --- # This vector represents a "No Difference / Marginal Benefit" scenario. # P(-2)=0.1, P(-1)=0.15, P(0)=0.5, P(+1)=0.15, P(+2)=0.1 my_probs <- c(0.1, 0.15, 0.5, 0.15, 0.1)  # --- 2. Set the number of samples --- # For example, simulate a cohort of 1000 patients. num_patients <- 1000  # --- 3. Generate the sampled scores --- qol_draws <- sample_qol_scores(prob_vector = my_probs, n_samples = num_patients)  # --- 4. View the results --- # Look at the first few sampled scores head(qol_draws) #> [1]  0  0 -2  1 -1 -1  # Check the distribution of the generated samples. # It should approximate the input probabilities. table(qol_draws) / num_patients #> qol_draws #>    -2    -1     0     1     2  #> 0.108 0.166 0.473 0.157 0.096

title: Summarizes the final utility score with advanced dynamic weighting. — summarize_final_utility
text: function calculates final weighted utility score. incorporates sophisticated weighting policy adapts based detected efficacy profile ('Cure' vs. 'Survival'). 'Survival' profile, weight 'cure' component scaled observed magnitude, preventing weak signal diluting score. cases, weight 'QoL' component also scaled magnitude, preventing neutral QoL diluting score. "unused" weight gradual adjustments redistributed proportionally among active components.
